findings.evidence: Figure 3.4 caption: "The figure's ~23 GB label for the two active experts is their resident weight (2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 GB, rounded to 23 GB); the 25.6 GB per-token read adds the ~2.8 GB of always-on attention/shared weights (1.4B × 2 bytes)."
findings.issue: The caption correctly explains the 23 GB vs 25.6 GB distinction, but the figure itself shows 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)' and 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on' while also showing 'per token: top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB'. The figure juxtaposes a resident 23 GB label (for the two active experts' weights) with a 25.6 GB per-token read label without a visual separator between the 'resident' and 'read' accounting lines. The caption reconciles them, but the figure alone is ambiguous about which number is memory and which is traffic. This is a minor figure-clarity issue, not a numeric error.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a one-line figure annotation or bracket separating 'resident weight' from 'per-token read traffic' so the 23 GB and 25.6 GB labels cannot be read as competing estimates of the same quantity.

findings.evidence: Page 55 (Fig 3.4 caption): "1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)" and "MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on"; the body text above the figure reads "per token: top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB".
findings.issue: The figure's own arithmetic is internally inconsistent: 8 experts × 11.4 GB = 91.2 GB of experts plus the always-on block gives 91 + 3 = 94 GB resident, but the always-on block is stated elsewhere in the same chapter as ~1.4B params (≈2.8 GB at FP16), not 3 GB — and the figure's own body text uses 1.4B/25.6 GB for the active read (11.4 GB + 2.8 GB = 14.2 GB, not 25.6 GB). The caption's later gloss tries to patch this: "The figure's ~23 GB label for the two active experts is their resident weight (2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 GB, rounded to 23 GB); the 25.6 GB per-token read adds the ~2.8 GB of always-on attention/shared weights (1.4B × 2 bytes)" — but 22.8 + 2.8 = 25.6 GB only if the 11.4B figure is 2 × 5.7B experts, which contradicts the figure's stated "top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B". A reader cannot reconcile 2 × 5.7B (=11.4B) + 2.8 GB with a 25.6 GB read without silently recomputing 12.8B × 2 B = 25.6 GB, which is a different decomposition from the one printed.
findings.fix_instruction: Fix the Fig 3.4 panel arithmetic so the always-on block is consistently ~1.4B params ≈ 2.8 GB (not 3 GB), and rewrite the per-token read line so it reads 'per token: 2 experts = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B active → 25.6 GB read (12.8B × 2 B)' rather than splitting 25.6 GB as '23 GB + 2.8 GB' while simultaneously printing 11.4B + 2.8 GB as the component sum.
